The grant type stored in the client session context comes from the raw grant_type form parameter. That value can only reach a successful token issuance after the token endpoint has resolved it to a registered grant, so an arbitrary value cannot get through. If a value did have no registered shortcut, encodeTokenId would throw rather than issue a token with a bad ID. The removed Context copy constructor has no remaining callers. response.consequence: The updated event assertions no longer verify that the token id was issued by the expected grant type. A token id carrying the wrong grant shortcut passes these tests, so the regression coverage this change adds is ineffective. Fixing only the offset would make every correct id fail.
response.explanation: In `isAccessTokenId`, the line `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two bugs. First, the condition is inverted. It rejects the token when the shortcut matches, and it never rejects when the shortcut differs. Second, the offset is wrong. Token ids look like `trltcc:1234` or `ofrtro:5678`, as the new DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest shows. The two-character grant shortcut is at indices 4-5, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`. `substring(3, 5)` returns the last character of the token type plus the first character of the shortcut, for example `tc` or `tr`. That value never equals a real shortcut such as `ac`, `rt` or `dg`. Because of this, the check never fires. The matcher accepts any id of the form `xxx?yy:uuid`, whatever grant it came from. If the offset were fixed without fixing the inversion, every correct token id would be rejected. The matcher is used by `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken`.

// Grant type shortcut starts at character 4th char and is 2-chars long
                if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
replacement.text:
// Grant type shortcut starts at the 5th char (index 4) and is 2-chars long
                if (items[0].length() < 6 || !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;

response.explanation: The change sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE per grant in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse (used by authorization code, device and CIBA), in the resource owner password grant, in pre-authorized code, in standard token exchange and in refresh. I did not check getId values in the grant factories.
